kitBriefs.eric: Enemy attack down · incoming damage down · squad health up
kitBriefs.hilde: Attack and defense up · damage proc · damage-reduction proc
kitBriefs.jaeger: Damage proc · enemy lethality-reduction proc · health up
kitBriefs.zoe: Damage over time · attack up · damage-taken amplification
kitBriefs.saul: Defense and health up · lethality up
kitBriefs.amadeus: Lethality up · attack up · damage proc
kitBriefs.petra: Damage-taken amplification proc · attack proc · damage-reduction proc

lineups.title: A garrison that hits back
lineups.lesson: Zoe adds attack and damage amplification; Saul adds lethality as well as defense and health. This is a developed older core with outgoing damage support, not simply a weaker version of Eric’s kit.
lineups.comparison: Holding buys occupation time and reinforcement time. Compare outgoing damage too: a garrison that clears the rally can preserve more troops for the next defense.

lineups.title: Change the kit one slot at a time
lineups.lesson: Eric changes Zoe’s damage-oriented slot to enemy attack reduction, incoming damage reduction and health. Jaeger adds health and a chance to reduce enemy lethality. Those are different effects, not just higher-generation stats.
lineups.comparison: Compare Eric with your developed Zoe, and Jaeger with your developed Saul. Keep each replacement’s actual skill levels, stars, gear and widget visible; the generation label cannot settle the tradeoff.

lineups.title: A garrison built to survive
lineups.lesson: Eric’s reductions and health support, Hilde’s damage-reduction chance and Jaeger’s health support act across the squad. Their benefits are not confined to infantry, cavalry and archers respectively.
lineups.comparison: Compare with Zoe or Saul when return damage is the priority. A defender widget supports the role, but it does not make the whole kit an automatic winner.

lineups.title: Use the rally kit already developed
lineups.lesson: Amadeus adds attack, lethality and a damage proc. Marlin adds damage procs and enemy lethality reduction. Hilde supplies attack, defense and damage support, although her widget skill is for defenders.
lineups.comparison: A rally widget is one part of the comparison. Do not discard a developed Hilde solely because an underbuilt Petra has the matching widget role.

lineups.title: Compare Petra with the cavalry you built
lineups.lesson: Petra brings attack and enemy damage-taken amplification procs, incoming damage reduction and a rally attack widget. Compare these with Hilde’s actual skill levels and investment, rather than comparing hero names.
lineups.comparison: Survival support matters on attack too. Compare Petra with your developed Hilde using actual reports; the troop-only simulator cannot resolve the full hero tradeoff.

lineups.title: Damage support across the rally
lineups.lesson: These kits combine attack, lethality, damage and target damage-taken effects. Their rally widgets suit the role. This makes them candidates to compare, not proof that this trio wins every Gen 3 matchup.
lineups.comparison: Start with the heroes your lead has developed. A survival skill is not wasted simply because this is an attack; compare losses and surviving troops as well as damage.

joiners.lesson: At skill 5, Super Nutrients contributes 25% squad health. A reliable early PvP option on either side. It stacks across selected copies; his second attack skill does not transfer.
Taskforce Training contributes 10% defense and 15% health at skill 5. Its two effect families are useful when coordinating with other survival skills. His third-skill lethality is absent as a joiner.
Desert Eclipse contributes a guaranteed 20% enemy damage-dealt debuff at skill 5. Its different effect family makes it a PvP option to combine with health and defense support.
Holy Warrior contributes a guaranteed 20% enemy attack debuff at skill 5. His health and damage-taken skills belong to his leader kit and do not transfer as joiner skills.

His first skill provides 20% damage-taken reduction at skill 5. Sloth’s testing rates this below Gordon’s 25% health contribution; do not read four copies as 80% fewer casualties. His second enemy-attack debuff does not transfer.
Stand of Arms contributes up to 25% lethality. It supports outgoing damage in PvP, but his second survival skill does not transfer. Yeonwoo and Amadeus supply the same first-skill stat family.
Tri-Phalanx contributes up to 25% attack. It adds a different offensive stat family from Chenko’s lethality; it is damage support rather than an automatic Castle joiner assignment.
